claims.text: Adding a minor amount of Ni to the Cu matrix mitigates phase separation in a W–Cu composite.
Adding a minor amount of Ni to the Cu matrix mitigates W–Cu interfacial void formation.
Ni addition improves thermal-conductivity retention under relevant heat-transfer and irradiation conditions compared with an untreated W–Cu composite.
The starting W–Cu composite is susceptible to interfacial degradation during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Ni introduced into the Cu phase modifies the W–Cu interfacial chemistry.
Ni segregates to the W–Cu interface.
Interfacial Ni improves bonding between W and Cu.
Interfacial Ni lowers W–Cu interfacial energy.
Ni acts as a wetting agent at the W–Cu interface.
Ni acts as a diffusion barrier that reduces atomic interdiffusion at the W–Cu interface.
Reduced interdiffusion suppresses interfacial-void formation and coalescence.
Reduced interdiffusion suppresses phase separation that would otherwise degrade thermal conductivity.
The Ni-modified composite will have a more stable and homogeneous interfacial region than the undoped composite after exposure.
Lower interfacial void density will lead to improved retention of thermal conductivity.
An equivalent W–Cu composite without Ni develops more pronounced phase separation and interfacial voids under similar conditions.
The intervention is applicable when homogeneous Ni distribution in the Cu phase can be ensured.
The anticipated benefit applies at moderate heat flux and irradiation conditions typical of plasma-facing-material joints.
Performance at significantly higher irradiation doses or under extreme thermal gradients is unverified.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule is logically malformed: it says the hypothesis is refuted if the Ni-modified material fails to reduce void formation while still retaining higher thermal conductivity. Higher retained conductivity supports the principal predicted outcome, so this conjunction does not provide an unambiguous refutation and does not state what follows if neither improvement occurs.
